India's onshore wind potential much higher than estimated, hits 2,933 GW at 200 m 2026-11-03 08:45:57 am | Source: IANS Bihar couple turns entrepreneur under PMFME scheme; their noodle business employs a dozen people News By Tags | #Industry #Bihar #SanjayKumar #RanjanaKumari #PMFME A couple from Sheikhpura district of Bihar, namely Sanjay Kumar and Ranjana Kumari , have become the talk of town over their food venture under the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme , and its capacity to employ about a dozen people in a short span of time. The couple, after learning about the scheme, received monetary support under the scheme and launched a noodle-manufacturing business not long ago. The initiative not only made their family financially self-reliant but has also created job opportunities for others in the surrounding area. Today, their entrepreneurial venture employs a total of 10 people regularly. Ranjana Kumari, sharing the success story of 'Smriti Noodles,' shared with IANS the difficult times when it was difficult to cover household expenses and manage children's education. Facing a weak financial situation, she aspired to start a venture of her own. It was during this period that she learned about the PMFME scheme. She applied under the program and, with government assistance, took the first steps toward establishing her business. Earlier a homemaker and now a successful businesswoman. Ranjana and her husband’s story has become an inspirational tale in the village as the family has not only become self-reliant but also employs locals in the noodle manufacturing business. She says that both men and women are currently employed at her unit. Expressing gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, she remarked that the scheme has served as a vital support system for women like her. Today, the family is not dependent on others to run expenses and is effectively fulfilling the family’s responsibilities. Ranjana’s husband, Sanjay Kumar, shared that his wife had long aspired to start a business, but rising inflation and household expenses made it difficult. It was during this time that they learnt about the PMFME scheme. With government assistance, they were able to install the necessary machinery and begin the production of noodles. According to Sanjay, this venture has given them, particularly his wife, a new identity. They are now receiving orders for noodles from several nearby districts, including Nalanda,

bihar_raw_news.title: NBCC Bihar Projects to Deliver 3,331 Homes and Tech Park - NewsIP
bihar_raw_news.content: (03.11.26 – By NewsIP Bureau – Patna) “All without any burden on the State exchequer,” NBCC (India) Limited Chairman and Managing Director Dr. K. P. Mahadevaswamy said of four redevelopment projects planned in Patna under Phase I. The projects are expected to provide 3,331 homes, Bihar’s first Tech Park and modern commercial spaces. Also Read: Business news Four projects planned across Patna NBCC signed memoranda of understanding with departments of the Government of Bihar for the four projects, which cover about 34.34 acres. The signing took place in August, but the source information does not specify the year. Chief Minister Sh. Samrat Choudhary, Deputy Chief Ministers Sh. Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Sh. Bijendra Prasad Yadav, and UDHD Minister Sh. Nitish Mishra were among those present. Also Read: Government and corporate appointments 3,331 homes across income groups Two residential projects will redevelop Bihar State Housing Board sites at Sector 5 (TV Tower) and Sector 6 (Bahadurpur). Together, they are planned to provide 3,331 flats for EWS, LIG, MIG and HIG categories, alongside facilities including shopping areas, clubhouses, gyms, community spaces and offices. Tech Park and commercial development A proposed IT Tech Park for DIT Bihar at Gardanibagh is described as the state’s first. NBCC says it is intended to attract IT companies, startups and investment, while supporting local employment and skills development. The other commercial project is planned at a Water Resources Department site on Bailey Road and includes hotels and commercial spaces. Estimated project value and employment Expected sale and lease proceeds from the four projects are estimated at about ₹5,152 crore, while the tentative project cost is about ₹2,000 crore, excluding GST. The source says the projects require no budgetary assistance from the state government. These are estimates, not reported project outcomes. A NBCC estimates around 40,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities across construction and operational phases. Its breakdown includes construction jobs and related supply-chain work, more than 5,000 direct jobs expected at the Tech Park, and additional jobs in residential, hotel and commercial operations. The figures are projections supplied for the projects. Green construction and next phase NBCC says the developments will incorporate measures such as rooftop solar, LED lighting, rainwater harvesting, wastewater treatment and reuse, and green landscaping. It cites its redevelopment work in New Delhi, including New Moti Bagh, East Kidwai Nagar and Nauroji Nagar, as relevant experience. Proposals for a second phase involving the Building Construction Department, Patna Municipal Corporation and Bihar Urban Infrastructure Development Corporation are at the approval stage, according to the supplied information. NBCC says MoUs with those departments are expected to be signed shortly. Also Read: NBCC to Develop Maharana Pratap Tourist Circuit at Haldighati

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of Pune Metro projects worth around 21,800 crore rupees today through video conferencing. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The Prime Minister will inaugurate Pune Metro Line 3, also known as the Pink Line, built at a cost of over 8,300 crore rupees. The project represents an important step towards strengthening Pune’s urban mobility infrastructure through technological innovation and modern transportation solutions. Spanning approximately 23 kilometres, the Pink Line connects Maan to District Court Metro station. The corridor will provide Metro connectivity between the Hinjewadi IT hub and Shivajinagar, improving access to one of Pune’s major employment centres and facilitating the daily commute of thousands of IT professionals and other commuters. The corridor will integrate with the existing metro network, providing seamless connectivity across different parts of Pune. It will help reduce dependence on private vehicles, ease traffic congestion and vehicular emissions, and improve access to major commercial and residential areas. A notable feature of the Pink Line is its emphasis on women’s empowerment and gender-inclusive public transportation. The line will be operated entirely by women train operators, making it a first-of-its-kind initiative. The project also emphasises environmental sustainability, with approximately 30 per cent of its total electricity requirements envisaged to be met through solar power. Mr Modi will also lay the foundation stone of Phase-II of Pune Metro, to be developed at an estimated cost of around 13,500 crore rupees. Phase-II comprises Pune Metro Lines 2A, 2B, 4 and 4A, which will substantially expand the city’s Metro network and strengthen connectivity across important residential, commercial and IT hubs. Under Phase-II, Lines 2A and 2B will span a total length of around 12.75 kilometres. Line 2A will connect Vanaz to Chandani Chowk, while Line 2B will connect Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi, extending the existing east-west Metro network. Line 4, spanning around 25.52 kilometres, will connect Kharadi to Khadakwasla. Line 4A, spanning 6.12 kilometres, will connect Nal Stop to Manik Baug. The new Metro corridors will connect several important locations, including Kharadi, Magarpatta, Hadapsar, Swargate, Manik Baug, Nanded City, Pune Cantonment and Warje. The eastern extension from Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi will improve connectivity to rapidly developing residential, commercial and IT hubs in Kharadi and Wagholi. The corridors will integrate with intercity bus services and the existing Pune Metro network through interchange facilities at Swargate, Nal Stop and Kharadi Bypass, facilitating seamless connectivity across different parts of the city. These projects will strengthen Pune’s public transportation infrastructure, improve connectivity across the city and provide commuters with an efficient and integrated urban mobility network.

national_raw_news.title: Unbeaten India register fifth successive win in Asian Champions Trophy Punjab 2026, set up semi-final clash against Korea
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Men’s Hockey Team completed an unbeaten league-stage run at the Hero Asian Champions Trophy Punjab 2026 on Monday with an 8-0 win over Korea – their fifth in a row – at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar. Dilpreet Singh (8′, 40′) scored twice, while Jugraj Singh (11′), Harmanpreet Singh (15′), Shilanand Lakra (33′), Sukhjeet Singh (34′), Sanjay (36′) and Angad Bir Singh (60′) were also on target. India finished at the top of the standings with five wins from five matches and will face Korea again in the semi-finals as the tournament moves to Mohali, where the semis will be played on November 4 and the medal matches on November 5. Second-placed Japan will face Malaysia, who finished the league stage in third place, in the other semi-final. India began aggressively in front of a packed house and created an early chance through Sukhjeet, whose backhand effort in the fourth minute was saved by goalkeeper Kim Jaehyeon. Dilpreet opened the scoring in the eighth minute with a backhand finish after a move that began with an aerial pass from Jugraj. India doubled their lead through a penalty corner in the 11th minute, with Jugraj scoring after Harmanpreet’s initial effort was kept out and Vishnukant Singh set up Jugraj on the rebound. Harmanpreet added another penalty-corner goal to his tally in the 15th minute to give India a 3-0 lead at the first break. He now tops the scoring chart with nine goals. Korea showed more intent in the second quarter and earned a number of penalty corners, but the Indian defence kept them at bay. Pathak also denied Son Dain in a one-on-one situation in the 27th minute with a timely save using his outstretched foot. India had opportunities of their own, but Aditya Arjun Lalage’s shot went wide, while another penalty corner did not result in a goal after the ball was ruled to have been played with the back of the stick. India went into half-time with their three-goal advantage intact. India increased the tempo after the break and added four goals in the third quarter. Shilanand Lakra scored in the 33rd minute after a penalty-corner variation. Harmanpreet’s pass found Jugraj, whose attempt was saved by Kim, but Lakra was on hand to put away the rebound. Sukhjeet made it 5-0 a minute later, deflecting Aditya’s pass from the baseline into the net. Sanjay added another in the 36th minute, reacting quickest after Dilpreet’s attempt was saved. India’s seventh goal came in the 40th minute when Sanjay controlled Harmanpreet’s long aerial pass and struck towards goal, with Dilpreet getting a touch to send the ball past the goalkeeper. India eased the tempo in the final quarter, with Korea enjoying periods of ball-possession but struggling to create clear chances. Suraj Karkera made a save when Korea threatened, while a penalty corner in the 58th minute came to nothing. Angad Bir Singh then scored a superb solo goal in the 60th minute, winning possession in the midfield, driving towards the circle and pushing the ball underneath the advancing goalkeeper to complete the 8-0 win. Korea had another penalty corner in the closing seconds, but failed to make the most of it. Sanjay, who was named ‘Player of the Match’, said India were pleased to finish at the top of the pool. “We wanted to top the table and we did that. We are very happy. I want to request the crowd to support us the same way in Mohali,” he said. India finished with 15 points and a goal difference of +29. Japan ended second with 10 points, followed by Malaysia with nine and Korea with six points. -IANS

national_raw_news.title: “Huge honour for India,” says Rijiju as Bhutan dedicates Stupa 76 to PM Modi
national_raw_news.content: Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Sunday expressed gratitude towards Bhutan after the King of Bhutan dedicated Stupa number 76 to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Rijiju represented India at the ceremony for raising and consecrating 108 Stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City. In an X post, he wrote, “It’s a huge honour for India that very sacred stupa 76 is dedicated to Hon’ble PM @narendramodi ji for his outstanding vision and commitment to friendship between India and Bhutan. On the auspicious occasion of Lhabab Duchen, joined the sacred ceremony in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan, marking the raising and consecration of 108 stupas, accompanied by the blowing of Dungchens.” “Paid my respects and offered prayers in the presence of His Majesty the King of Bhutan, Her Majesty the Gyaltsuen, H.E. Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Prime Minister of Bhutan & the people of Bhutan. A deeply meaningful spiritual occasion, reflecting Bhutan’s rich Buddhist heritage and the enduring bonds of friendship between our two nations,” he added. According to the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Rijiju conveyed gratitude on behalf of Prime Minister Modi to the King of Bhutan for the gesture of dedicating a Stupa as part of the Project. The 108 Stupas project was conceived by the King of Bhutan, who also steered its implementation. In a single day, thousands of volunteers erected 108 Stupas, each 15 metres tall and separated by 108 metres on an 11.7 kilometre stretch along the Aie (Mau) River within Gelephu Mindfulness City near the border with Assam. The project aims to showcase Gelephu Mindfulness City as a prominent centre of Vajrayana Buddhism, while simultaneously representing the values and culture of the Bhutanese people, the ministry stated. Earlier today, Rijiju called on Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay in Gelephu, where the two leaders held “warm and very positive” discussions aimed at strengthening the India-Bhutan partnership and exploring the potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City project. “Delighted to call on H.E. Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Hon’ble Prime Minister of Bhutan, in Gelephu today. Had a warm and very positive discussion on India-Bhutan partnership, and the immense potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City for both nations. India remains a steadfast partner in Bhutan’s path of growth and prosperity,” Rijiju posted on X. The Union Minister is on a visit to Bhutan from October 31 to November 2. The two sides have maintained a healthy trend in bilateral cooperation in diverse areas including development cooperation, trade, energy, investment, connectivity and cultural connections. -(ANI)
